title: Shelach: as grasshoppers (Numbers 13:33)
hookLine: "we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight"

lines: PEOPLE READ HOW WE HOLD OURSELVES.
cards: A candidate sits in the hallway before a job interview, already sure he's the least qualified person in the building. When he's called in, his shoulders drop. He talks too fast and apologizes before answering.
The person across the desk, who had no opinion of him a minute ago, starts to form one, based on the one he walked in with. It isn't magic. People read how we hold ourselves.
Twelve scouts come back from forty days in the land, carrying grapes, and ten of them deliver a report with a line people still quote.

teach.b: The report starts out true. The land does flow with milk and honey, they say, and here's its fruit. Then comes the word but.

The people there are strong; the cities are walled and very large. As the crowd grows uneasy, the report darkens. Ten of the scouts now say the land devours its inhabitants, and everyone there is huge.
Then the line: there we saw the Nephilim, the giants, "and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight." Two halves. The first is honest: we felt tiny.
The second is a guess dressed up as a fact. How could the scouts possibly know what the people of the land thought of them?

teach.h: WHO TOLD YOU HOW THEY SAW YOU?
teach.b: A midrash imagines God catching exactly this: I don't mind that you felt like grasshoppers, but who told you how I made you look in their eyes?
The Talmud gives the scouts a little evidence: they overheard the locals say there are ants in the vineyards that look like people. But the book of Joshua tells a different story.
A woman in Jericho named Rahab tells two new spies that terror of Israel has fallen on her land, ever since they heard how the sea dried up before them.
Their hearts melted. The people the scouts feared were afraid too. The scouts saw a fact, big people in walled cities, and let a feeling write the rest of the report.
Their picture of themselves became the picture they gave everyone else.

how: Teachers often take up the scouts' line about grasshoppers when Shelach is read; they use it, and the midrash on it, to talk about self-image, and about the difference between what we see and what we assume.

o: the giants the scouts said they saw in the land
send: the portion where the scouts report back
the spies Joshua later sent to Jericho

games.q: the scouts' report — tap the pairs.
p: milk and honey, and its fruit

s: the scouts said the land was poor and barren
they said it flowed with milk and honey, and showed its fruit, then added "but."
the verse claims to know how the land's people saw the scouts
"and so we were in their sight": a guess stated as a fact.
the book of Joshua says Jericho had no fear of Israel
Rahab says the city's hearts melted when they heard of Israel.

games.q: later, in the book of Joshua, two new spies hide in Jericho. a woman named Rahab tells them how her city has felt about Israel. what does she say?
o: they laugh at Israel; they're like grasshoppers.
they've been terrified; their hearts melted.
games.why: Joshua 2: the people of the land were afraid of Israel. the scouts' guess about how others saw them was wrong.

practice: Think of one situation coming up that makes you feel small, a meeting, a family dinner, a room full of people who seem bigger, and notice the picture of yourself you're already carrying in.
Then separate the two halves the way the verse does: what do you actually feel, and what are you only guessing they'll think? Let the guess go, just for a minute.

wordCard.voice: Shelach, the scouts' portion. Today: grasshoppers in our own sight, and the guess that others saw us the same way.

orig.note: Hebrew: like grasshoppers. how the scouts saw themselves.

carryVoice: Your line: how you see yourself shows. A feeling isn't a report on what others see. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.

sources.ref: Talmud Bavli, Sotah 35a; Rashi on Numbers 13:33
